text:
sasha: heads up — after the v2.3.1 rollout we're seeing a consistent tail latency regression (p95/p99) on 8k token workloads, ~12-18% on canary hosts.

ci-bot: [PERF][canary] regression detected for v2.3.1: baseline p99 92ms -> current 110ms (+19%). link: https://ci.internal/reports/17582

derek: saw the alert, running a bisect on canary image set now.

lin: i already started collecting KV-cache metrics; eviction rate is up on the same hosts.

ana: can you paste a sample from the cache logs? curious about reuse patterns.

lin: sure — snippet:
```
kv_cache: evict_count=1247, hit_count=8423, miss_count=1120, avg_kv_size=258
policy: dynamic-window(80ms)
```

derek: bisect results so far: regression lands between merge A (PR 421) and merge B (PR 428). PR 421 changed kernel selection heuristics (wmma fallback), PR 428 adjusted adaptive batching window and added an experimental batching timeout.

sasha: which one is the more likely culprit?

derek: initial flamegraphs point to increased overhead in the batcher hot path after 428 — more small batches, less dense batching. also KV eviction aligns with the same timeframe.

elise: timeline makes sense: 428 reduced the batch wait to favor latency which kicked more small batches through and disabled an opportunistic merge path that relied on kernel-level fusion from 421.

ana: so two changes interacting -> emergent regression. classic.

sasha: propose rollback PR 428 from canary and run canary perf suite again. if that fixes, we revert 428 and then reopen with smaller scoped fixes.

elise: I'm +1 on rollback. opening rollback now.

rollout-bot: rollback initiated for deployment v2.3.1-canary at 1758205123 by elise. status: in_progress

ci-bot: perf-run queued against rollback candidate. link: https://ci.internal/job/1758205

derek: while rollback runs, i started a targeted microbench to reproduce kernel selection vs batcher interplay. script below (local):
```
./bench --seq-len 8192 --batcher=adaptive --kernel-policy=autoselect --reps=50
```

lin: microbench shows p99 back to baseline when we simulate pre-428 batch window. KV eviction drops ~70%.

ci-bot: perf-run complete: rollback candidate shows p99 93ms (+1%) — within threshold. link: https://ci.internal/job/1758205/result

rollout-bot: rollback complete. canary scaled back to pre-428 image at 1758205740.

sasha: good. immediate mitigation done. next: post-release retro and CI hardening.

elise: retro notes so far — root cause: emergent interaction between batcher adaptive-window change (PR 428) and kernel-selection fallback (PR 421) causing more small batches and higher KV churn. fix strategy: revert 428, then reintroduce smaller changes behind feature flag and add safety checks.

derek: actions i'm taking:
- PR 450: add microbench for kernel-selection x batch-window matrices (seq len sweep). link: https://git.internal/r/450
- PR 451: increase sample size for perf CI and pin CPU governor in runners to reduce noise.

lin: my actions:
- PR 452: kvcache-smoke that simulates long convo and asserts eviction rate < 5% after warmup.
- add metric: kv_cache_eviction_rate to perf dashboard with alerts.

ana: test tuning: tighten acceptable regression threshold for p99 to 6% (was 10%), add median+p95+p99 checks to reduce flakiness.

elise: also found one flaky perf test that sometimes flipped due to background cleanup job. PR 453 disables that job in CI runners during perf jobs.

sasha: solid. please add short bullet points to the postmortem doc and include reproduction steps and commits involved.

elise: will create the postmortem doc and tag infra/qa for follow up. google doc: https://docs.internal/reports/perf-retro-17582

derek: follow-up: once PRs land, i recommend a gradual canary with telemetry gating — only promote if p99 delta < 4% and kv eviction < 3%.

sasha: agreed. thanks everyone for the quick triage and good diagnostics :thumbsup:

elise: i'll post summary in #eng-releases and schedule a short retro tomorrow.

ana: leaving notes for ops: monitor kv_cache_eviction_rate and batch_size_distribution for next 72h.

ci-bot: created perf-issue ticket TICKET-987 for tracking.

sasha: closing thread here. we'll re-open if anything pops up.
